problem:
5x + 4y + 6z = 47
2x + y + 3z = 26
If (x, y, z) is a solution to the given system of equations, what is the value of x + y + z?

bad.why: Subtracting the second equation from the first (3x + 3y + 3z = 21) and dividing by 3 is the hand derivation that one bracket regression and a sum line replace.
Computing (47 - 26)/3 needs the student to see that the difference of the equations is 3(x + y + z): elimination done in the head.
Typing (47-26)/3 into Desmos is arithmetic on a combination the student derived; Desmos removes none of the math.

algebraFirst.description: Subtracts the second equation from the first (3x + 3y + 3z = 21), notices every coefficient is 3, and divides by 3.

explanationNotes: Explain that one bracket regression fits both equations at once, that x and y are typed x_1 and y_1 because Desmos uses them for the graph's axes, and that the fitted x_1, y_1, and z are only one of many solutions while x + y + z is the same for every one of them. The trap choices are 21 (forgetting to divide by 3) and 73 (adding the two equations).
